item.description: The European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR) is an award-winning international think-tank that aims to conduct cutting-edge independent research on European foreign and security policy and to provide a safe meeting space for decision-makers, activists and influencers to share ideas. We build coalitions for change at the European level and promote informed debate about Europe’s role in the world. In 2007, ECFR’s founders set about creating a pan-European institution that could combine establishment credibility with intellectual insurgency. Today, ECFR remains uniquely placed to continue providing a pan-European perspective on some of the biggest strategic challenges and choices Europeans need to confront, with a network of offices in seven European capitals, over 90 staff from more than 25 different countries and a team of associated researchers in the EU 27 member states. For more information check our website: ecfr.eu

item.title: Associate
item.description: We don’t just talk, we do. Lead the change with us. At the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, we work with political leaders around the world to drive change. We help governments turn bold ideas into reality so they can deliver for their people. We do it by advising on strategy, policy and delivery, unlocking the power of technology across all three. And by sharing what we learn on the ground, so everyone can benefit. We do it to build more open, inclusive and prosperous countries for people everywhere. We are a global team of over 800 changemakers, operating in more than 40 countries, across five continents. We are political strategists, policy experts, delivery practitioners, technology specialists and more. We speak more than 45 languages. We are working on over 100 projects, tackling some of the world’s biggest challenges. We’re all here at TBI to make a difference. In a world of ever more complex challenges, we believe diversity of background and perspective is a strength. We pride ourselves on a culture that values and nurtures difference. We are dedicated to unlocking potential, not only for the countries we work in but also for each of our team members. No matter where you’re from or who you are, if you’re passionate about the transformative power of progressive politics, we invite you to build a better future with us. Role Summary TBI is supporting the Government of Kazakhstan in delivering an ambitious agenda focused on economic growth and attracting foreign investment. The Associate will play a pivotal role in designing and providing workstreams in priority economic sectors, working directly with high-level government counterparts in the Presidential Administration, key ministries, and key financial institutions, alongside global TBI experts. This is a 12-month fixed-term contract with the option to extend. Associates represent most of our teams worldwide and have access to excellent career opportunities. Whether they are at TBI for a small or large share of their career, as Associates progress within the Institute, they are exposed to opportunities to contribute to projects that generate impact at scale. Key Responsibilities ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Associates must be able to operate with clients and across TBI with professionalism, confidentiality, integrity, and tact. Their key responsibilities include the following: Technical Leadership Conduct research and data analysis to inform recommendations on existing and future government policies and programs. Keep abreast of industry trends, data sources, and developments to provide clients with the best advice. Analyse the effectiveness of government policies and programs and develop recommendations for improving such policies and programs. Conduct error-free and timely analysis using an appropriate medium (e.g., PowerPoint and Word) in client-friendly language and with visuals. Project & Team Management Contribute to the success of TBI’s start-up office in Kazakhstan through building local networks, supporting improvement of operations and processes, and building up a positive team culture that reflects TBI’s values. Key Requirements Professional experience in one or more of the following areas: investment, foreign direct investment (FDI) attraction, industrial policy/economic competitiveness, and/or energy and infrastructure. 4+ years of experience as a political staffer, multi-lateral staff, or in civil society organisations. Alternatively, 2+ years of experience in a top-tier management consulting firm. Demonstrated ability to dissect complex, messy problems into clear insights and pragmatic solutions - equally comfortable with qualitative nuance and quantitative rigour. Learns fast, asks sharp questions, and translates research into data-backed recommendations that move the needle for leaders. Rolls up sleeves to get work done - drafts, briefing notes, models, interviews, travels - whatever it takes; never hides behind titles. Stays optimistic and steady under pressure, turning setbacks into fuel rather than complaints. Navigates ambiguity with discipline, prioritises experiments, and delivers on time even when the path forward isn’t obvious. Sets big goals for personal growth and for client impact, measures success by outcomes, not activity. Proactively spots opportunities to expand the mandate, raise the bar, and create outsized value for all stakeholders. Generous teammate who listens first, challenges ideas (not people), and elevates those around them. Communicates crisply - whether in a hallway chat or a board-level deck - and treats every interaction as a chance to build trust. Proficiency in Russian is considered a strong asset, and Kazakh is a plus. We reserve the right to close this role early if we receive a sufficient number of applications. Closing Date:

item.description: Senior Policy Advisor, UNFCCC, London, Brussels or Berlin E3G is recruiting a Senior Policy Advisor to advance our work around UNFCCC and climate diplomacy. This is an exciting time to join E3G and build the next generation of climate diplomacy and engagement for the organisation that will be critical in spurring action and impact. The Senior Policy Advisor role will be based from either our London, Brussels or Berlin office, with a preference for London. Context The global climate regime is entering a new phase. With the core framework for implementing the Paris Agreement now largely in place, the priority must be to accelerate implementation and ensure that international cooperation delivers real-world progress on mitigation, adaptation, resilience and finance. At the same time, geopolitical turbulence, economic uncertainty, energy security concerns and growing pressure on public finances are reshaping the conditions for international cooperation. The UNFCCC remains central to global climate action, but needs to evolve to support delivery in this new context. This means strengthening the links between negotiations and real-economy action, making greater use of coalitions and partnerships where they can deliver progress, and connecting climate diplomacy with wider economic, energy, trade, finance and development agendas. The period to the second Global Stocktake (GST2) in 2028 will be critical to demonstrating progress, building confidence in international cooperation and creating the conditions for stronger action through the next NDC cycle. Background E3G is a world leading strategy think tank on the political economy of climate change with a global outlook. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate for all. Our goal is to translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policy makers to account on their promises. E3G’s diplomatic work extends across the whole climate regime, including the UN negotiations and cooperation on the energy transition, financial reform, green industry, trade and increasing resilience. E3G particularly focuses on understanding and influencing the connections between climate politics and global agendas in foreign, security and economic policy. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top-ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. E3G offers a dynamic and fast paced working environment that will value your insight, initiative and collaboration wherever you are in the organisation. Role Overview It is against this backdrop that E3G is recruiting a highly versatile and experienced practitioner to serve as Senior Policy Advisor for UNFCCC. This position will lead the UNFCCC engagement work within a dynamic, high-powered, and highly visible multi-location team within the Climate Diplomacy & Geopolitics (CDG) division of E3G and will have a particular goal of advancing E3G climate diplomacy goals and objectives in international fora including the UNFCCC process, COP, at the UN and beyond. This position requires deep experience working within the UNFCCC framework, ideally with a track record for influencing and solid personal network in this space. It will be responsible for building and cultivating critical relationships within governments, across international negotiations and relevant fora, and across the broader stakeholder community, as well as driving relevant political analysis, research, advocacy, and communications initiatives with key foreign policy actors and institutions to drive ambitious effective climate cooperation in multilateral venues. The role will also work closely with relevant E3G teams around thematic issues such as finance, trade,industry, energy transition, adaptation and resilience which are critical areas to shape international climate cooperation. It will report to Programme Lead, Climate Diplomacy & Geopolitics, and work closely across CDG and the organisation. You would be responsible for line management of a small team, including at least one Policy Advisor and/or researcher. Person Description You are a highly motivated and intellectually curious international climate policy professional with the ability to work quickly and creatively across complex issue sets, disparate actors and policy agendas, and different coalitions to identify and develop solutions and diplomacy pathways toward climate cooperation and impact. You pride yourself in building and maintaining trusted relationships across the foreign policy community and are committed to high quality outputs even when under pressure. You excel at fostering and nurturing a team and working across teams and issue areas to yield the greatest impact. Experience and Skills The successful candidate will also be able to demonstrate: At least seven years of experience working in the fields of one or more of: foreign policy, climate change policy, international relations, negotiations. Experiences of building consensus across countries and stakeholder groups around sensitive issues ; creating and facilitating dialogue and agreement. Demonstrable experience w orking on international climate policy and international issues in both analytical and influencing roles, including ideally in multilateral contexts and venues related to climate . Experiencing working with and on the UNFCCC process is highly desirable. Ability to operate confidently at high and “expert” level, in the worlds of government, business, the media and civil society. Used to operating internationally , with a high degree of cultural sensitivity. Strong personal networks at international level would be an advantage. Track record of thought leadership and problem solving, including authorship of significant reports and comment pieces. Experience managing complex projects , line management , and donor relationships. Commitment to achieving E3G’s objectives, and to working in an innovative and entrepreneurial manner. item.description: Policy Advisor, International, Climate Diplomacy & Geopolitics, London, Brussels or Berlin E3G is looking for a Policy Advisor to support its Climate Diplomacy and Geopolitics Programme (CDG) in driving forward our multilateral engagement work. The Policy Advisor will be based from either our London, Brussels or Berlin office, with a preference for London. Background E3G is an independent climate change think tank with a global outlook. We are world leading strategists on the political economy of climate change, dedicated to achieving a safe climate for all. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate. Our goal is to translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. Context The international system is entering a period of profound change. Geopolitical competition, economic uncertainty, conflict, energy security concerns and pressure on public finances are reshaping the conditions for international cooperation, while climate change and the transition to a low-carbon economy are increasingly intertwined with questions of economic security, development and global stability. In this context, effective climate action will depend on strengthening and adapting multilateral cooperation across institutions and fora. The UNFCCC and Paris Agreement remain central, but progress will also depend on how climate priorities are advanced through wider regional and global institutions, existing and emerging coalitions and partnerships as well as traditional major groupings such as the G7, G20 and BRICS. item.description: Role Summary TBI is seeking a Country Security Manager (CSM) for Ukraine to provide effective, proportionate, and high-quality security support to our TBI Ukraine team. This role reports to the Head of Operational Capability, based in London, with a technical reporting line to the Ukraine Country Director, and will work closely with colleagues across TBI's global operations and Duty of Care functions. The postholder will be the principal in-country security adviser, supporting the Country Director and TBI in discharging Duty of Care responsibilities through practical security risk management, preparedness, business continuity, and incident coordination. This is a locally based role in Kyiv, Ukraine. TBI is not able to sponsor, obtain or facilitate a reservation or deferment from mobilisation in connection with this position. Applicants must be able to independently meet the requirements of the position in accordance with applicable Ukrainian law and their individual mobilisation obligations. Appointment to, or employment in, this role does not alter an individual's mobilisation status or provide protection from mobilisation. Key Responsibilities Core Areas Act as the principal in-country security adviser, supporting the Country Director and TBI's Duty of Care responsibilities in Ukraine. Implement TBI's Global Duty of Care Policy and associated security requirements in Ukraine, working with Operational Capability/HQ to harmonise country arrangements with global standards. Maintain and embed the Ukraine Essential Security Package (ESP), including the Country Risk Register, Welcome Pack, SOPs, HRE Plan and contingency arrangements. Provide timely, concise and decision-focused security advice that translates developments in the operating environment into practical implications and actions for TBI. Maintain preparedness for incidents, business continuity disruption and seasonal risks, including winterisation. Build a positive security culture through staff briefings, onboarding, exercises and practical engagement. Maintain strong external security networks and coordinate specialist external support when required. Proactively escalate material risks, incidents, capability gaps and support needs to the Country Director and Operational Capability/HQ. Duty of Care, Governance and Global Standards Support the Country Director in implementing TBI's Global Duty of Care Policy and associated security requirements in Ukraine. Work closely with Operational Capability/HQ to ensure Ukraine's security arrangements remain aligned with TBI's global security standards, policies and risk-management approach. Translate global requirements into practical and proportionate country-level arrangements appropriate to the Ukrainian operating environment. Maintain effective technical coordination with Operational Capability/HQ, including escalation of material risks, incidents, capability gaps and changes in the operating environment. Participate in global security assurance, review, and quality-assurance processes as required, and implement agreed improvements. Identify where local conditions require adaptation of global approaches and work with Operational Capability/HQ to agree on appropriate solutions. Contribute lessons, emerging risks and good practice from Ukraine to the continued development of TBI's global Duty of Care and security capability. Security Continuously monitor and analyse the security context in Ukraine, with particular attention to conflict and aerial threats relevant to TBI personnel, operations and planned activity. Produce concise, timely and practical security updates for staff and leadership, clearly explaining what has changed, why it matters to TBI and whether action is required. Distinguish between general security reporting and developments that materially affect TBI's operational exposure and provide proportionate mitigation advice. Maintain and update the Ukraine Country Risk Register in accordance with TBI's global risk-management methodology. Maintain and embed the Ukraine ESP, SOPs, HRE Plan, emergency contacts and contingency arrangements, ensuring they remain aligned with global requirements. Ensure staff understand prevalent threats, security procedures, incident reporting and escalation routes, and their individual responsibilities for security. Provide proportionate security planning and advice for staff movements, programme travel, leadership visits and events, ensuring arrangements reflect the operating environment and TBI’s actual risk exposure. Build and maintain an active security network in Ukraine, including INSO, OSAC, embassy security teams, peer organisations, relevant authorities, emergency services and reputable providers. Resilience Support the Country Director and Operational Capability/HQ to maintain appropriate crisis-management, business-continuity and contingency arrangements for Ukraine. Coordinate security-related winter preparedness and monitor infrastructure disruption affecting staff, accommodation, communications, transport and office continuity. Ensure contingency plans are regularly reviewed and exercised, including HRE, evacuation, relocation and hibernation arrangements where applicable. Act as the principal in-country security focal point during incidents, coordinating initial response, staff accountability, communications and escalation. Provide timely analysis and practical options to decision-makers during incidents and support TBI crisis-management arrangements when activated. Lead or support after-action reviews and ensure lessons are incorporated into country procedures and, where relevant, shared with Operational Capability/HQ. Training and Engagement Deliver regular, practical security briefings and security onboarding for staff and visitors. Plan and deliver tabletop exercises and other proportionate security exercises to test procedures and build staff confidence. Promote a positive security culture based on shared responsibility, preparedness and practical risk awareness. Communicate security requirements in a way that is accessible, proportionate and relevant to TBI's operating environment. Representation and Coordination Act as a trusted critical friend to the Country Director and leadership, providing clear advice that enables programme delivery while appropriately managing risk. Draw on TBI resources and specialists to deliver high-quality technical advice and avoid operating as a standalone country function. Maintain strong working relationships with Operational Capability/HQ and contribute to harmonisation of Ukraine systems and practices with global standards. Coordinate specialist external capabilities, including emergency evacuation support, secure transport, or surge operational support, when required. Represent TBI professionally with internal and external stakeholders and maintain high standards of integrity, discretion and confidentiality. Role Boundaries TBI requires a lean, information-led and proportionate security capability appropriate to its operating model. This is not a close protection role. Person Specification The ideal candidate will combine strong security risk-management experience with excellent judgment, communication skills, and an understanding of how security enables an advisory organization to operate. They will be able to filter a complex security environment and provide senior leaders and staff with concise, proportionate, and practical advice. This is a role requiring an exceptional candidate: With at least five years' relevant security risk-management experience, the majority of this experience is from a volatile or conflict-affected environment. Who has a strong understanding of the legal, moral and organisational dimensions of Duty of Care and experience implementing security policy and standards at country level. item.description: Full time, fixed term contract with probation period. Power to Prosper is a national community wealth building programme, delivered by the New Economics Foundation (NEF) in partnership with a network of community hubs across the UK. The programme works to build community-owned economic power and challenge racial and economic inequality. While we establish Power to Prosper as an independent organisation it is being incubated within the New Economics Foundation group and contracts of employment will be offered on a fixed-term basis only via NEF Consulting. As Senior Community Organiser, you will build organised community power across Power to Prosper’s Hubs. You will identify and develop leaders, build strong relational networks, support communities to identify shared issues, undertake power analysis, develop strategy and organise collective action that can secure meaningful change. You will also develop the organising capacity of Hub organisations and other organisers, helping to build strong local teams that can act together over the long term. The purpose is not simply to increase participation in Power to Prosper, but to build the leadership, relationships and collective power communities need to shape and increasingly own their local economies. Important: Community organising is a specific craft and discipline within Power to Prosper, and previous experience of practising community organising is a non-negotiable requirement for this role. We will not accept experience in community engagement, participation, co-design, outreach or community development as a substitute. These are valuable disciplines in their own right, but they are distinct from community organising and will not be considered equivalent experience for this role. Applicants must have been trained in and have practised community organising, including building relationships and collective power through purposeful one-to-ones, identifying and developing leaders, deep listening, power analysis, strategy, public action and negotiation. Our organising practice is informed by traditions and methodologies associated with Saul Alinsky and Marshall Ganz, as well as comparable power-based organising approaches. Applicants must be able to demonstrate hands-on experience of practising this specific craft, rather than simply an understanding of organising principles or related community-based work. You will identify and develop leaders, build strong relational networks, support communities to identify shared issues, undertake power analysis, develop strategy and organise collective action that can secure meaningful change. You will also develop the organising capacity of Hub organisations and other organisers, helping to build strong local teams that can act together over the long term. The purpose is not simply to increase participation in Power to Prosper, but to build the leadership, relationships and collective power communities need to shape and increasingly own their local economies. Important: Community organising is a specific craft and discipline within Power to Prosper, and previous experience of practising community organising is a non-negotiable requirement for this role. We will not accept experience in community engagement, participation, co-design, outreach or community development as a substitute. These are valuable disciplines in their own right, but they are distinct from community organising and will not be considered equivalent experience for this role. Applicants must have been trained in and have practised community organising, including building relationships and collective power through purposeful one-to-ones, identifying and developing leaders, deep listening, power analysis, strategy, public action and negotiation. Our organising practice is informed by traditions and methodologies associated with Saul Alinsky and Marshall Ganz, as well as comparable power-based organising approaches. Applicants must be able to demonstrate hands-on experience of practising this specific craft, rather than simply an understanding of organising principles or related community-based work. item.title: Associate Director, Clean Economy, London, Brussels or Berlin
item.description: Associate Director, Clean Economy, London, Brussels, Berlin. Clean Economy at E3G E3G is an independent climate think tank working globally to achieve a safe climate for all. We work on the politics of climate change, translating climate politics, economics and policy into action at national and international levels. Our 2026–2030 strategy positions E3G for a disrupted world in which industrial competitiveness, trade and economic security have become the terrain on which climate outcomes are decided. The Clean Economy strategy aims to create the political conditions for accelerated industrial transition, manage trade tensions and make new industrial and trade partnerships possible. E3G's standing rests on political economy analysis, scenario work, advocacy and campaigning; on sectoral depth in steel, cement and chemicals and across carbon border measures, trade agreements and investment regimes; and on a trusted convening role with governments, international initiatives and civil society networks. Clean Economy is a growth area for E3G and its scope is widening as the politics move. Geo-economics is the first direction. Governments increasingly pursue national advantage through markets, money and technology, using tariffs, export controls, investment screening and sanctions alongside cooperative instruments such as trade agreements, harmonised standards and supply chain arrangements. As multilateral institutions weaken, cooperation is being rebuilt in plurilateral and public-private form, shifting the question from how countries reduce dependence to how they govern interdependence. E3G already works this terrain through investor-state dispute settlement, trade regime reform and economic security; building it out is a cross-cutting endeavour drawing on climate diplomacy, geopolitics and political economy expertise across our European, international and Asia arenas. Industrial policy and clean tech supply chains is the second. Europe's clean energy build-out depends on inputs concentrated in a small number of producers, with China controlling the large majority of the battery value chain, rare earth refining and permanent magnet production. EU and UK industrial strategies have set objectives without setting a framework for deciding what to build domestically, what to source from trusted partners, and where security considerations justify higher-cost diversification. Developing E3G's position here calls for close collaboration with energy, geopolitics and political economy colleagues across arenas, and is a priority for cross-cutting capability investment. These are political choices about industrial strategy, trade and security, and E3G has the political economy analysis, the convening role and the government access to shape how they are made. The Opportunity Clean economy is one of the most contested and consequential areas of climate politics right now. This role at E3G puts you at the centre of it. Industrial strategy, trade and economic security have moved from the margins of the climate debate to its core, and E3G is uniquely positioned to shape how governments, industries and international institutions navigate that shift. This is a 12-month maternity cover appointment carrying the full accountability of the Associate Director role — strategic direction, funding, people and impact of the Clean Economy theme. The brief during this period is genuinely strategic and developmental: to take a theme that is already doing important work and extend its reach into geo-economics and clean tech supply chains, working collaboratively with E3G's climate diplomacy, geopolitics and political economy colleagues across our European, international and Asia arenas — in the context of E3G's 2026–2030 strategy. The postholder will have real scope to shape and build the team — contributing to new hires, influencing how emerging roles are defined, and building Clean Economy's Asia capability. The theme goes into the cover period with strong programme leadership and a clear strategic direction. The opportunity is to build on that and hand it back in a stronger position than you found it. This role sits in E3G's Senior Management Team and wider Senior Leadership Team. If you are ready to lead at the level of strategy and organisational development — and to do it in one of the most dynamic areas of the climate politics landscape — we want to hear from you. You will bring: Strategic leadership: The ability to set direction, hold accountability for outcomes, and lead through others rather than owning everything directly. Facilitative and lateral leadership: Working across teams, petals and organisational boundaries to achieve shared goals; enabling others rather than directing. Leading leaders: Developing and managing senior programme leaders with confidence, holding accountability while empowering delivery and development and building a broad leadership base. External profile and influence: Representing E3G at institutional level; holding senior relationships with funders and partners; shaping debate in the industry, trade and economic policy field. You will have significant experience in the industrial transition, trade, industrial policy or economic security field — in think tank, policy, institutional, government or related settings — and a track record that demonstrates both intellectual leadership and the ability to deliver at scale. item.description: Role Summary The global financial system is undergoing a significant transformation, driven by digital assets, stablecoins, tokenisation, programmable money, and emerging financial infrastructure. The Policy Analyst – Geoeconomics & Digital Assets will conduct research and analysis to support TBI’s work on these developments and their implications for governments. The postholder will contribute to high-quality policy research examining how emerging financial technologies and changes in the international financial system affect national resilience, economic competitiveness and strategic influence. They will help translate complex economic, technological and geopolitical developments into clear analysis and practical policy recommendations. Working with colleagues across TBI, the Analyst will contribute to policy papers, briefings and other analytical products and, under supervision, support engagement with governments, regulators, central banks, academics, international organisations and industry stakeholders. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policymakers to account on their promises. E3G’s diplomatic work extends across the whole climate regime, including the UN negotiations and cooperation on the energy transition, financial reform, green industry, trade and increasing resilience. E3G focuses on understanding and influencing the connections between climate politics and global agendas in foreign, security and economic policy. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. Excellent research and analytical skills, including the ability to learn quickly, gather, synthesise, assess evidence and reach well-founded conclusions. Capacity Building and Technical Assistance Contribute to the development of technical tools, guides, and operational materials; Participate in the design and facilitation of training activities for regional teams, health districts, and operational teams; Provide technical support during supervision and monitoring missions; Support the integration of nutritional approaches and SRMNIA-N into family planning interventions; Promote the sharing of experiences, the dissemination of best practices, and the application of lessons learned. Partner Coordination Contribute to coordination with technical and financial partners working in the areas of SRMNIA-N and family planning; Participate in technical working groups and sectoral consultation forums; Monitor joint actions and partner commitments; Support the alignment of partner interventions with the priorities of the DSME and the MSHP. Candidate Profile Education A minimum of a master’s degree (Bac +7) in nutrition, public health, maternal and child health, medicine, pediatrics, epidemiology, or any other relevant field; Additional training in health program management, monitoring and evaluation, or reproductive health is a plus. Professional Experience A minimum of seven (7) years of experience in implementing or coordinating programs in maternal health, nutrition, SRMNIA-N, or family planning; Proven experience in coordinating and monitoring public health programs; Experience collaborating with the MSHP, and technical and financial partners; Experience in analyzing program data and monitoring performance; Field experience at the regional or health district level is a major asset; Good knowledge of Senegal’s healthcare system. Technical Skills Good knowledge of policies, strategies, regulatory frameworks, and international standards related to SRMNIA-N and family planning in Senegal; Proficiency in integrated PPFP/SRMNIA-N approaches; Excellent analytical, synthesis, and writing skills; Proficiency in monitoring and evaluation, reporting, and data analysis tools; Proficiency in office software and health information systems; Proficiency in nutrition data processing software; Proficiency in using data from nutrition surveys, food security surveys, and demographic and health surveys. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- French version Aperçu Le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique (MSHP), à travers la Direction de la Santé de la Mère et de l’Enfant (DSME), met en œuvre le projet « Renforcement de la coordination des services publics de planification familiale au Sénégal » afin d’améliorer la qualité, l’intégration et la performance des services de planification familiale et de santé reproductive. Dans le cadre de ce projet, la DSME bénéficie de l’appui de la Delivery Unit du MSHP (DU-MSHP), chargée de renforcer les mécanismes de coordination, de suivi de la performance et de résolution des goulots d’étranglement affectant la mise en œuvre des priorités stratégiques du secteur. Afin de soutenir cette dynamique, nous recrutons un(e) Expert(e) en Nutrition et Santé Maternelle et Infantile chargé(e) d’apporter un appui technique à la DSME pour renforcer l’intégration de la planification familiale post-partum (PPFP) dans les services de santé reproductive, maternelle, néonatale, infantile, adolescente et nutritionnelle (SRMNIA-N), conformément aux orientations du Plan Stratégique National SRMNIA-N 2024-2030. Expert(e) en Nutrition et Santé Maternelle et Infantile sera sous la tutelle technique de la DSME et travaillera en étroite collaboration avec la DU-MSHP. Le recrutement s'effectuera dans le cadre d'un contrat de consultance d'une durée d'un an, renouvelable sous réserve d'une évaluation satisfaisante des performances. Objectif du poste Appuyer la DSME dans la coordination technique, le suivi de la performance et l’intégration des approches nutritionnelles et SRMNIA-N dans les interventions de planification familiale et de PPFP afin d’améliorer la qualité, la continuité et l’utilisation des services dans les régions prioritaires. Les objectifs spécifiques sont les suivants : Appuyer la stratégie de l’intégration de la PPFP dans les services de santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et nutritionnelle ; Appuyer la DSME dans l’identification et la résolution des goulots d’étranglement affectant la qualité et la continuité des services ; Contribuer à la mise en œuvre du dispositif de coordination et de suivi de la performance porté par la DSME et la DU-MSHP ; Appuyer l’exploitation des données programmatiques afin d’améliorer la prise de décision ; Renforcer les capacités des équipes régionales et opérationnelles sur les approches intégrées PPFP/SRMNIA-N. Responsabilités clés Coordination technique et appui à la décision Appuyer la DSME dans la coordination technique des interventions intégrées PPFP/SRMNIA-N ; Participer à l’élaboration, à la mise à jour et au suivi des plans d’actions et priorités opérationnelles ; Préparer les réunions techniques, revues de performance et cadres de coordination ; Produire des analyses techniques, notes de synthèse et recommandations stratégiques destinées à la prise de décision ; Contribuer à l’élaboration et à la mise à jour des guides, protocoles et outils de gestion ; Veiller à l’alignement des interventions avec les politiques, stratégies et priorités nationales du MSHP. Suivi de la performance et amélioration de la qualité des services Assurer le suivi des indicateurs clés relatifs à la nutrition, à la santé maternelle et infantile ainsi qu’à la PPFP ; Analyser les données programmatiques afin d’identifier les écarts de performance et les opportunités d’amélioration ; Identifier les contraintes opérationnelles affectant la qualité, la disponibilité et la continuité des services ; Contribuer au suivi de la mise en œuvre des plans d’actions correctifs ; Assurer la collecte, l’analyse et l’utilisation des données pour le suivi des indicateurs ; Appuyer la documentation des résultats, des progrès réalisés et des enseignements tirés de la mise en œuvre ; Participer aux missions de supervision, de suivi et d’évaluation dans les régions prioritaires. Renforcement des capacités et assistance technique Contribuer à l’élaboration d’outils techniques, guides et supports opérationnels ; Participer à la conception et à l’animation d’activités de formation destinées aux équipes régionales, aux districts sanitaires et aux équipes opérationnelles; Fournir un appui technique lors des missions de supervision et de suivi ; Accompagner l’intégration des approches nutritionnelles et SRMNIA-N

item.title: Finance Manager
item.description: Role Summary The Finance Manager will play a critical role in providing financial insights and ensuring compliance across finance and tax. The role will be responsible for overseeing the central management accounting function, owning key areas of the balance sheet reconciliations, supporting the account’s payable function, and ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting with strong financial control. The role will also support the Head of Tax and International Finance across TBI’s Tax requirements. Key Responsibilities Management accounts: Support the month-end process including management accounts, accruals, prepayments, payroll, and reviewing cash reconciliations. Find efficiencies to reduce the month-end close. Own the balance sheet reconciliation process, ensuring accurate and timely reconciliations. Work closely with the Accounts Payable function and support the use of technology and AI to ensure accuracy. Support FP&A with variance and performance analysis and assist with budgeting & forecasting. Day-to-day oversight of project cash requirements, including being a key point of contact with external stakeholders and managing the approval of payments. Actively engaging and communicating with the senior finance team. Maintain strong financial control processes, ensuring compliance with internal policies and control frameworks with the central and regional finance teams. Tax Compliance & reporting: Prepare the quarterly UK VAT return for review by Head of Tax. Work with AP and Workday teams to introduce improvements to the process of VAT handling within TBI to increase efficiency of VAT compliance processes. Support the Head of Tax with collaboration between tax and finance, including VAT recovery and cost centre coding. Support the use of technology and AI within the VAT processes where practical. Preparation of finance information suitable for supporting tax compliance processes such as annual corporate income tax returns prepared by external advisors. Including analysis of sensitive spend categories. Prepare the Corporation Tax, WHT and VAT balance sheet reconciliations. Prepare the Tax note in the consolidated and UK financial statements. Prepare the local monthly tax calculation. Support the Head of Tax with the tax timetable and own the production of the tax accounts. Develop practical documentation, process notes, and controls to improve resilience and reduce reliance on individual knowledge. Financial reporting: Support the Head of Central Finance on the preparation of the consolidated group accounts, subsidiary accounts, managing the reporting timetable and the external audit. Support the intercompany process and reconciliations. Help build robust rules around legal entity discipline including which entity incur costs, how those costs are allocated, how the recharge process works and how transfer pricing then applies. Support the Head of Tax on transfer pricing processes and preparing for the new UK transfer pricing information requirements (International Controlled Transactions Schedule). Ensure up to date and accurate technical accounting compliance with accounting standards. Support the Head of Central Finance to develop new policies, process notes, and training when there are changes to accounting standards. The above list of job duties is not exclusive or exhaustive, and the post holder will be required to undertake such tasks as may be expected within the scope of the post. Person Specification The Tony Blair Institute for Global Change aims to equip political leaders and governments to build open, inclusive, and prosperous societies in an interconnected world. We do this by developing policies and advising governments. This is a role in a fast-paced team, working within complex divisions that are highly scrutinised. Therefore, the successful candidate for the role should be able to display most of the following: ACA or International Equivalent qualification. Trained at a professional service firm. Relevant experience in all areas of consolidated financial statements, reporting under UK GAAP (FRS 102) and IFRS. Experience in preparing statutory financial statements and managing external audits. 5+ years of experience in finance or accounting roles, with a focus on financial reporting, management accounting and tax. Some technical understanding across UK and international tax is desirable. Experience working in a global organisation with exposure to multiple currencies and international operations. Proactively contributes to the implementation of best practice guidelines and methodology for Finance policies and processes. Proficiency in financial modelling and analysis using excel and financial software. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact with stakeholders at all levels of the organisation. An understanding of banking systems. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and adapt to changing priorities. Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy in financial reporting and analysis. Must be able to take ownership and manage their own workflow with minimal input from management, set their own goals and plan how to achieve them – translate into actions and follow through to completion, prioritise against tight deadlines. Takes an active interest in the work that the Institute undertakes. Closing Date: 2026-10-25

item.title: Director of Tax and International Finance
item.description: Role Summary Reporting directly to the Chief Financial and Operating Officer, the Director of Tax and International Finance will provide senior leadership and strategic direction across TBI’s Tax, International Finance and Travel teams. The role will develop the direction for these areas, strengthen governance and controls, and ensure high-quality delivery through the teams it leads. TBI has a complex international tax and finance footprint arising from the breadth of its operations, the number of jurisdictions in which it works and the range of tax, statutory and compliance obligations that follow. The Director will ensure that TBI has a sustainable, well-controlled and proactive approach to managing these obligations and the associated financial risks. A key priority will be to continue maturing the operating model: moving beyond core compliance and reactive issue management towards stronger risk management, clearer accountability, better use of data and systems, more resilient regional support and greater value to the wider organisation. The role will also provide senior finance leadership during periods of Finance change, working closely with the Financial Controller and other Finance leaders to ensure clear ownership, effective hand-offs and appropriate segregation of duties across Tax, International Finance and related processes. The role is expected to evolve with TBI’s needs. The principal responsibilities are set out below. Key Responsibilities Tax Develop and deliver TBI’s overall tax strategy, governance and risk management framework, ensuring tax implications are considered appropriately as TBI’s geographic footprint and activities evolve. Provide senior oversight of UK and international tax matters, including corporation tax, VAT and other indirect taxes, employment taxes, withholding tax and transfer pricing, working closely with HR, Legal, Payroll and Finance colleagues where responsibilities intersect. Ensure proportionate tax controls, review processes, documentation and segregation of duties are embedded across key tax processes. Oversee the preparation, review and timely submission of key tax filings and tax accounting outputs, with clear accountability between Tax and Financial Control for preparation, review and approval. Manage relationships and risks with HMRC and overseas tax authorities, including audit readiness, enquiries and responses. Provide strategic advice on tax implications of new country entry, organisational change, cross-border arrangements and other significant business decisions. Reduce reliance on external advisers where appropriate by building internal capability, ownership and institutional knowledge, while using specialist advice where it adds value or mitigates material risk. International Finance Lead the International Finance team, providing strategic direction, technical support, escalation, people leadership and a strong connection into the wider Finance function. Own the control environment and risk oversight for regional finance activity across MENACA, APAC, the Americas and Africa, setting clear standards and expectations for regional teams. Oversee key International Finance outputs, including balance sheet reconciliations, bank payments, month-end deliverables and other material control activities, with review and approval calibrated to risk. Be accountable for the effective coordination of local statutory accounts, audits, direct and indirect tax compliance, withholding and payroll taxes, transfer pricing disclosures and new-country finance requirements, working through regional finance managers and external advisers as appropriate. Strengthen central oversight of regional finance activity, reducing key-person dependency and improving resilience, documentation and continuity of local knowledge. Work with FP&A, Financial Control and regional teams to clarify roles, responsibilities, hand-offs and escalation routes, supporting a well-run global Finance function. Ensure alignment across tax, statutory reporting, transfer pricing, intercompany arrangements, treasury-related processes and group audit requirements. Travel Lead the Travel Team, ensuring effective, service-oriented and well-controlled travel operations, including policy compliance, supplier management, duty-of-care support and reporting. Improve travel management information, spend visibility, policy compliance, exception management and the performance management of travel suppliers and the travel management company. Work with relevant stakeholders to ensure travel policy and processes remain proportionate, practical and aligned with TBI’s global operating model. Leadership, Controls and Transformation Lead continuous improvement across Tax and International Finance, working closely with Financial Control, Operational Finance, AP, Payroll, HR, Legal, Technology and regional teams. Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce manual intervention, improve workflows and strengthen the quality, consistency and accessibility of tax and finance data. Drive effective use of Workday and other technology, including appropriate AI-enabled solutions, with a focus on strong underlying processes, controls and data quality. Develop clear management information and risk reporting that enables senior stakeholders to understand material tax, international finance and travel risks, trends and priorities. Build capable, engaged teams with clear objectives, accountability, development plans and succession resilience. Raise the profile of Tax, International Finance and Travel as proactive, pragmatic and value-adding partners to the wider organisation. Person Specification The successful candidate will be able to demonstrate: Substantial senior leadership experience spanning tax and finance in a complex international organisation. Strong technical knowledge of UK and international tax, with the judgement to identify, assess, prioritise and manage risk across multiple tax areas and jurisdictions. Significant experience of international finance, including statutory reporting, audit, local compliance and the operation of finance teams across multiple jurisdictions and regions. A strong understanding of financial controls, governance, risk management and process improvement, with experience strengthening operating models and control environments. The ability to operate strategically while remaining sufficiently close to the detail to identify risk, challenge effectively and drive delivery. Experience of finance systems and data-led process improvement, with a practical understanding of how technology and automation can improve finance operations. Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the credibility to work effectively across Finance, HR, Legal, Payroll, Technology, regional teams and senior leadership. A strong track record of leading and developing teams through change, providing clarity, continuity and direction while building capability and accountability. Pragmatic commercial and professional judgement, with the ability to balance risk management, operational delivery, cost and organisational context. Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex tax and finance matters clearly and succinctly to non-specialists and senior decision-makers. A proactive, improvement-focused mindset and a track record of moving functions from reactive compliance delivery towards more mature, insight-led and value-adding models. A recognised professional accountancy qualification; a recognised tax qualification would be advantageous. Desirable Experience working in a not-for-profit, international development, government advisory or other mission-led organisation. Experience with Workday or a comparable global finance system. Experience leading finance transformation, automation or AI-enabled process improvement. Experience overseeing travel operations, travel compliance, duty of care or supplier management. Closing Date: 2026-10-25
